K14 What a Sync writes (US-270-03a, §5.3). A catalogue that is too large, not UTF-8 JSON, not schema 1 or holding too many items fails the whole Sync. Each item is checked on its own, and a refused item is counted and never written: its package path is exactly '/api/marketplace/catalog/files/<its digest>/package.autotheme' (or an https URL under 'https://github.com/AutomatosAI/automatos-design-kit/releases/download/', §5.4's allowlist); base64-decoded themeJson hashes to files['theme.json'].sha256 and passes contract.parse_json + manifest.validate_manifest (package.py:396-403's reading) with the item's id and version; digest.digest_of_manifest(files) (:47-49) equals the item's digest and the envelope's; and signed_upload.check_upload_signature(db, CheckedThemePackage(manifest, {}, files, digest), envelope bytes) verifies (signed_upload.py:156-174: it reads only the manifest's id and version, the digest and the file manifest, so a package with no files checks the Sync's metadata exactly as an upload's; a key the revocation feed revoked is refused there too). Accepted items are written in ONE transaction: a theme id held here by any local-origin Marketplace row (the operator's own listing) is skipped whole and counted refused, because all_listings groups versions by theme id (listings.py:148-154) and a Cloud version would otherwise be offered to, and auto-update, that local listing's installs (§5.3: never overwritten); an item whose digest a Marketplace row already holds is unchanged; a theme not held before is new; a newer version of a Cloud theme is updated. A Cloud row: theme_id, version, owner_type 'marketplace', workspace_id NULL, digest, manifest (the checked theme.json), file_manifest (the item's files), storage_prefix storage.theme_prefix(theme_id, version) (storage.py:38-43; one Marketplace row per version, uq_theme_packages_marketplace_version, themes.py:196), status 'approved', reviewed true, scan_verdict 'not_run' (this install ran no scan; the signature is the review's proof), signature (the envelope's), source 'cloud', submitted_by NULL, plus one theme_review_events 'approved' row (actor NULL, detail {source: 'cloud'}; THEME_REVIEW_EVENTS is not a CHECK, themes.py:104-105). Any database error rolls back every row and records last_attempt_at and last_error only (revocation_pull._failed :263-275's pattern): the last good Sync stays. A private upload (owner_type 'workspace') is never touched. Forward compatibility: an item whose `type` is not 'theme' is skipped, never refused and never a reason to fail the Sync (W2 adds other types to the same schema-1 catalogue).

Likewise pull._run_sync (:244-249) fetches the catalogue with the MANAGE dependency's reads still open. updates._fetched (:127-141) already does it right: expunge the row, roll back, then download. userStories.title: A Sync counts only a unique-index collision as 'written meanwhile'; any other integrity error fails the Sync
userStories.description: LOW (review of 7a0ff63f3). As the operator, I want a bug in the row a Sync builds to fail the Sync with its plain error, never to show up only as a refused count.
acceptanceCriteria: CAUSE: pull.write_item (:179-193) catches every IntegrityError as 'another Sync or a submission wrote that version or digest meanwhile' and the item is counted refused with a warning, so a CHECK (ck_theme_packages_source, the status CHECK), NOT NULL or foreign-key violation, which is a bug in _cloud_row, is swallowed as a count instead of rolling the Sync back with NOT_SAVED (AGENTS.md: never swallow an error). Also apply_catalog (:221-223) adds the item to held (held.with_item) even when the write was refused, so a second catalogue entry with that digest reads 'unchanged' though nothing was written. → DONE — cause confirmed as stated: write_item's bare except IntegrityError counted every integrity error (a CHECK, NOT NULL or foreign key as well as a unique index) as written meanwhile, and apply_catalog called held.with_item even after a refused write, so a later copy of that digest read unchanged. Fixed in commit 27426c0e6 (orchestrator/services/marketplace_cloud/pull.py).

CHANGE: write_item treats only a unique violation as 'written meanwhile' (the DBAPI error's pgcode '23505', or its constraint name being one of theme_packages' unique indexes) and re-raises any other IntegrityError, which _run_sync's SQLAlchemyError branch turns into _failed(NOT_SAVED) with nothing written; apply_catalog adds an item to held only when it was written. → DONE — pull.is_unique_violation reads the DBAPI error's SQLSTATE (psycopg2's pgcode, psycopg's sqlstate) against UNIQUE_VIOLATION '23505'; write_item re-raises any other IntegrityError after its savepoint rolls back, and _run_sync's SQLAlchemyError branch turns it into _failed(NOT_SAVED) (full rollback, last_attempt_at and last_error recorded, the last success kept); apply_catalog holds an item only when its verdict is still new or updated after the write. userStories.title: The public catalogue files route holds no pool connection over storage, and rebuilds a bounded number of packages at once
userStories.description: MEDIUM (review of 5aa6123a6). As the operator of the hosted edition, I want an unauthenticated caller of GET /api/marketplace/catalog/files/{digest}/package.autotheme to be unable to tie up the API's database pool, threads and memory, so a burst of package requests can't take the rest of the API down.
acceptanceCriteria: CAUSE: api/marketplace_catalog.get_catalog_file (:166-187) reads the version with served_version (:181) on get_db's session and then calls read_catalog_file (:186) with that read transaction still open, so the request holds a pool connection idle in transaction for the whole storage read. For package.autotheme that is catalog_files._package_file (:134-146) -> review_package.rebuilt_package: one S3 GET of every stored file, a sha256 of each and a deflate of the lot, up to THEME_MAX_PACKAGE_MB (32 MB), on every request without If-None-Match, with about two to three times the package in memory. The route is public, and its only bound is the per-IP limit (MARKETPLACE_PUBLIC_RATE_PER_MINUTE, 120 a minute; RateLimitStore fails open when Redis is down, and get_client_ip's first-X-Forwarded-For issue is already filed). About 30 concurrent package requests take every pool connection (core/database/database.py:85-86, pool_size 10 + max_overflow 20; other routes then wait pool_timeout 30 s) and most of FastAPI's threadpool, whatever the CDN in front does with the immutable Cache-Control. K9 chose a rebuild per request to avoid storing a zip; that stays. → DONE — cause confirmed as stated: get_catalog_file read the version with served_version on get_db's session and then called read_catalog_file with that read transaction still open, so every storage read (and the whole rebuild for package.autotheme) held a pool connection idle in transaction, and package rebuilds were bounded only by the per-IP limit. Fixed in commit e1543840a (orchestrator/api/marketplace_catalog.py, orchestrator/services/marketplace_cloud/catalog_files.py).

CHANGE: (a) get_catalog_file ends its read transaction before any storage read, as updates._fetched does (db.expunge the served row, then release_if_read_only or db.rollback), for a screenshot and for the package, so no pool connection is held while storage answers; the 304 path still reads nothing from storage. (b) Package rebuilds are bounded per process: a threading.BoundedSemaphore of a named constant (CATALOG_PACKAGE_REBUILDS, 2) with a short named wait; a package request that gets no slot in that wait is a 503 with Retry-After, FILE_REFUSAL_HEADERS and no-store (logged as a warning), the reader never called. Screenshots stay unbounded (one object each, capped by the manifest's screenshot cap). rebuilt_package, read_theme_package and every other K4 function stay byte-identical; the route's answers, headers and status codes don't change otherwise; no new dependency. → DONE — (a) api/marketplace_catalog._served_detached runs served_version under the route's refusals, then db.expunge(package) and db.rollback() (as updates._fetched does; the route only read), so the detached row keeps its loaded columns and the connection is back in the pool before listed_sha256, the 304 and any storage read, for a screenshot and for the package; the 304 path still reads nothing from storage. (b) catalog_files._rebuild_slot takes one of REBUILD_SLOTS = threading.BoundedSemaphore(CATALOG_PACKAGE_REBUILDS = 2) within REBUILD_SLOT_WAIT_SECONDS (1.0) around rebuilt_package and gives it back in a finally on every path; none free raises CatalogFilesBusy, which _file_refusals maps to 503 FILES_BUSY with Retry-After REBUILD_RETRY_SECONDS (5) on FILE_REFUSAL_HEADERS (SERVING_HEADERS + no-store), logged as a warning, the reader never called. Screenshots and 304s take no slot. rebuilt_package, read_theme_package, verified_file, read_stored_file and every other K4 function untouched; no new dependency. py_compile, check_changed_code_shape.py (0 errors), check_hierarchy_gate.py pass. code-reviewer and security-reviewer run in the foreground: nothing blocking; the code-reviewer's docstring LOW fixed. Left for the owner (the story's design, a bound, not a cache): the security-reviewer's MEDIUMs, one client keeping both slots busy so other package requests 503, and a served body (up to 32 MB) held until sent after its slot is released; and S3 reads use the STANDARD profile (boto's default timeouts and adaptive retries), so a hung read holds a slot that long (read_stored_file is K4 byte-identical). userStories.title: The public catalogue never queues its callers behind a build without a bound, and reads theme.json with no transaction open
userStories.description: MEDIUM (review of d4ace737c). As the operator of the hosted edition, I want a slow or failing object store to cost the unauthenticated GET /api/marketplace/catalog a quick 503 or a moment-old catalogue, not the API worker's threads and a pool connection idle in transaction, so a storage blip while the catalogue is cold can't stall the rest of the API.
acceptanceCriteria: CAUSE: services/marketplace_cloud/catalog.catalog_snapshot (:105-120) waits on `_building` (:113) with no bound, and the caller that holds it runs build_catalog (:117) on the route's get_db session: all_listings (via _items :129-134) and publisher_view (_item :161) open a read transaction that stays open while _theme_json_text (:195-211, verified_file over serve.read_stored_file :202, boto's default timeouts and retries) reads each listed version's theme.json from storage whenever the kept text is missing: after every restart or deploy, and for each newly listed version. With storage slow or failing at that moment, the builder holds a pool connection idle in transaction for every read; every other caller of the public route (each signed-out visitor's Themes tab on /marketplace, and every local install's Sync) parks one of the worker's threadpool threads on the lock with no limit; and a failed build keeps nothing (by design, test :347), so each waiter in turn takes the lock and repeats the whole build, and the queue drains at about one storage timeout per caller while the worker's other plain-def routes wait for threads. The same class as P270W1-RVW-5 on the files route, which bounds its wait (catalog_files._rebuild_slot :153, REBUILD_SLOT_WAIT_SECONDS) and ends its read transaction before storage (api/marketplace_catalog._served_detached :177-184).

CHANGE: (a) build_catalog(db, now) (the entry point test :347 patches) does every database read first (all_listings, catalogued_verdict, publisher_view per item), keeps the rows' loaded columns (db.expunge, as _served_detached does) and ends the read transaction (release_if_read_only, or db.rollback as _served_detached does) before reading any theme.json (the kept text first), then assembles the items; the catalogue's items, their order, every field and every refusal (SigningKeysError, CatalogUnavailable) stay as they are. (b) catalog_snapshot waits for `_building` at most a named constant (CATALOG_BUILD_WAIT_SECONDS, about 2 s: `_building.acquire(timeout=...)`, released in a finally); a caller that doesn't get it in time is answered the last snapshot this process holds, even one older than CATALOG_KEPT_SECONDS (a moment-old catalogue beats none; its body and ETag are its own, so the size cap and the 304 still apply), and when none is held raises a new CatalogBusy, which api/marketplace_catalog._snapshot answers 503 with Retry-After (a named constant) and REFUSAL_HEADERS (no-store), logged as a warning, with neither the database nor storage read for it. A failed build still keeps nothing and the next caller that gets the lock builds again. Every K4 function (serve.read_stored_file, serve.verified_file and the rest) stays byte-identical; no new dependency; the route's 200, 304, 404, 429 and 503 answers otherwise unchanged.

TEST (orchestrator/tests/test_prd270w1_catalog_feed.py): (1) with services.marketplace_cloud.catalog.read_stored_file wrapped by a reader that records the route session's in_transaction() on every call, a cold build reads every listed theme.json with no transaction open (FAILS on d4ace737c: True on every read); (2) while one build is held inside its theme.json read (the wrapped reader waits on a threading.Event the test sets afterwards), a second catalog_snapshot call on another thread returns within CATALOG_BUILD_WAIT_SECONDS plus a small margin: CatalogBusy when no snapshot was held, the reader not called by it (FAILS on d4ace737c: it waits for the build), and the held snapshot's body and ETag when an expired one was held; (3) a CatalogBusy from catalog_snapshot makes GET /api/marketplace/catalog a 503 with Retry-After and Cache-Control no-store; (4) every existing test in the file still passes, test_one_build_serves_every_caller_for_the_kept_seconds_and_a_failed_build_keeps_nothing (:347) included, unchanged.
userStories.notes: Raised by the code-reviewer (MEDIUM 1: the lock waited on with no timeout over cold-start storage reads) and the security-reviewer (2: a failed build is retried by every waiter in turn) of d4ace737c; confirmed by this pass's reviewer by reading catalog.py and api/marketplace_catalog.py, who added the read transaction held open over the storage reads. A negative cache of a failed build was considered and left out: the bounded wait already bounds the threads, and test :347's 'a failed build keeps nothing' stays as it is. The first-X-Forwarded-For limiter issue (api/credentials.get_client_ip) is already filed and is not this story.
